## ps2 — addressing the ps1 `LLM-Review -1` (finding accepted, not contested)

Reviewer finding (`attest.py:435`): the legacy-tolerance branch of the fail-closed guard was
untested — dropping the `and _signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest(auth_manifest)` conjunct
would not have been caught.

**Accepted as correct.** It is the same defect class this ticket investigated, pointed at my
own guard. The positive test proves the guard FIRES; nothing proved it does not fire where it
must not. A one-sided guard test cannot distinguish *"correctly fails closed on a degraded
basis"* from *"fails closed on everything"* — and the second would break every pre-S4b
attestation: a **fail-closed regression hiding inside a fail-open fix**. It is also the same
shape as the pre-existing pin criticised in the RCA, which asserted the fallback does not
crash but never asserted a verdict.

### Added

`test_pre_s4b_attestation_still_verifies_when_the_gate_ref_is_unresolvable` — a pre-S4b
attestation (no `verified_at_sha`, hashes produced against the working tree, so the working
tree IS its correct basis) under the **same unresolvable** gate ref must still verify
`ok=True` / `certified`.

Anti-vacuity, deliberately: it uses the unresolvable ref, not a resolvable one — a resolvable
ref would exercise a different arm entirely and pass for the wrong reason. It then asserts
`gate_ref_hash_basis(...).degraded is True` and that the signed manifest carries no
`verified_at_sha` **before** the gate call, so the first conjunct is proven satisfied and only
the legacy-tolerance conjunct can be holding the gate open.

### Mutation check — both directions, sandboxed, discriminating

| mutant | negative test | positive test |
|---|---|---|
| drop the legacy-tolerance conjunct (`if basis.degraded:`) | **FAIL** (rc=1) | pass |
| remove the guard entirely (`if False and …`) | pass | **FAIL** (rc=1) |

Each mutant dies to **exactly one** test, and neither test kills the other's mutant — the pair
is orthogonal rather than overlapping, which is stronger than "both die". Seed application was
grep-verified in source each time, not assumed; run under `sandbox-exec` with writes confined
to the worktree and scratch. Restored afterwards (`0 mutants remain`).

### Scope of ps2

**No production code changed between ps1 and ps2** — `git diff --stat src/` against ps1 is
empty. The delta is the one test. That also means the label copy condition could not treat it
as `NO_CODE_CHANGE`: on push Gerrit reported both `LLM-Review-1` and `Verified+1` as outdated
and removed, so the `-1` did not carry forward and the bot will re-review.

`make lint` (complexity ratchet included) and `make typecheck` (684 files) exit zero;
`test_ref_coherence.py` **8 passed**. Change-Id `Ia44373f9…` preserved via `make amend-msg` —
no duplicate change.
